humanities_role_explanation: Puns and jokes (SemEval-2017 Task 7, Context-Situated Puns, ExplainTheJoke) supply the items, but the paper tests a general prompting technique (adding TTS audio to text) for explanation quality, not disciplinary competence in humor studies or literary/linguistic scholarship. Humor is treated as a computational NLU target.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text jokes are paired with synthetic speech generated by OpenAI tts-1-hd; Gemini-1.5-Flash receives both text and audio in one prompt. Audio is not a native dataset modality but derived from text.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Models first decide whether a text is a pun or non-pun (humor detection) and produce chain-of-thought 'explanations' of why the joke is funny (humor explanation, phonetic ambiguity, homographic/heterographic puns). Explanations are judged by GPT-4o pairwise against human explanations or against each other (LLM-as-judge), which is closest to fact_verification of explanation quality.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to one task (humor/pun explanation) and one prompting method; no new benchmark introduced.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Gemini-1.5-Flash as generator; GPT-4o as judge; a Hugging Face open-source audio model (Gazelle) for logit analysis.

quantitative_metrics.note: Win rate and tie rate from pairwise LLM-judge comparisons.

published_after_march_2023.note: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Computational Humor, January 19, 2025.

summary: The paper proposes a training-free multimodal prompting approach in which an LLM receives both the text of a joke and a TTS-generated spoken version, to improve humor explanation. Evaluated on SemEval-2017 Task 7, Context-Situated Puns and ExplainTheJoke with Gemini-1.5-Flash and GPT-4o as judge, audio increases win rates across all datasets. Ablations and logit analyses probe phonetic ambiguity and voice effects.
key_findings: Adding audio improves win rates by roughly 4 points on SemEval (heterographs 47.76 to 51.74; homographs 68.89 to 72.59), also on Context-Situated Puns and ExplainTheJoke (12.81 to 15.44). Audio-only prompting is far worse than text-only; voice type has no clear systematic effect.
dataset_size: SemEval 2017 Task 7: 810 homographic + 647 heterographic puns + 1077 non-puns; Context-Situated Puns: 821 + 1739 puns; ExplainTheJoke: 350 jokes (several datasets; no single combined total)
gold_upstream: SemEval-2017 Task 7 (Miller et al., 2017) human annotations and explanations; Context-Situated Puns (Sun et al., 2022) annotations; ExplainTheJoke human explanations scraped from the website (theblackcat102). Production of these annotations is described only as 'human annotations' / 'human explanations'.
facets_explanation: The paper reuses three existing humor datasets: SemEval 2017 and Context-Situated Puns carry structured pun-word annotations, and SemEval and ExplainTheJoke carry human explanations. For ExplainTheJoke, whose human explanations vary 'in style, length, quality and accuracy', the authors had GPT summarize them to produce a more normalized reference, i.e. variability is treated as noise. Evaluation is by GPT-4o pairwise judgment rather than matching to a key.
results_explanation: Table 1 reports SemEval win rates with audio of 51.74 (heterograph) and 72.59 (homograph) versus a baseline of 47.76 and 68.89 against human explanations. The largest gap between input regimes is in the ablation (Table 4): audio-only 25.50 vs. 'Our System' 51.74 on heterographs, about 26 points; and audio-only 55.86 vs 72.59 on homographs. The largest reported gap among input regimes is therefore about 26 points, derived by subtraction. The 55 value above is incorrect and should be read as 26. No human baseline is reported as a number.

humanities_role.quote: we explore a simple multimodal prompting approach to humor understanding and explanation

dataset_size.quote: This set contains 810 & 647 puns (homographic & heterographic), and 1077 non-puns.
This broad collection of jokes was scraped from the ExplainTheJoke.com website, containing 350 jokes.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: In total, each prompt included six examples of pun explanation pairs

gold_source.quote: It contains human annotations: noting the pun-word and the spelling or definition of the pun-word in both interpretations of the pun.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: the presence of structured annotations for both pun datasets gave the judge ground-truth, so that it did not rely on its own understanding of the joke

answer_multiplicity.quote: The judge, GPT-4o, was then asked to output whether explanation 1 was better than explanation 2, explanation 2 was better than explanation 1, or whether both explanations were of equal quality.

plurality_treatment.quote: which themselves have high variability in style, length, quality and accuracy

reported_format_gap_kind.quote: finding that pure audio-only prompting performs far worse than pure textual prompting
